proof_skeleton_nl: Fix arbitrary integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, let q be an indeterminate, define R_{a,b,r}(q) as in the theorem, and assume R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q]. Fix an arbitrary integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2), where D = r(b-a). By Lemma L1, the coefficient [q^j]R_{a,b,r}(q) equals the coefficient [q^j]F_{a,b,r}(q) of the formal interval-product expansion. By Lemma L2, polynomiality of R_{a,b,r}(q) implies the divisibility-dominance inequalities M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d. By Lemma L3, [q^j]F_{a,b,r}(q) is the signed count of the subset-partition set X_j. Lemma L5, applied using the dominance inequalities and the degree bound j <= floor(r(b-a)/2), provides a sign-reversing involution on X_j whose fixed points all have positive sign. Lemma L4 then identifies the signed count with the number of fixed points, so the signed count is a nonnegative integer. Therefore [q^j]F_{a,b,r}(q) is a nonnegative integer, and hence [q^j]R_{a,b,r}(q) is a nonnegative integer as well. Since j was arbitrary in the allowed range, the theorem follows.

steps.derives: For the fixed admissible parameters a, b, r and the fixed integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2), if R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q], then [q^j] R_{a,b,r}(q) = [q^j] F_{a,b,r}(q), where F_{a,b,r}(q) = product_{i=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+i)) * sum_{m>=0} q^(m i)).
steps.trivial_justification: This is the final clause of Lemma L1 applied to the standing assumption R_{a,b,r}(q) in Z[q].

steps.derives: For every positive integer d, the interval-multiple dominance inequality M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b) holds.
steps.trivial_justification: Lemma L2 states exactly that polynomiality of R_{a,b,r}(q) implies these inequalities for all positive integers d.

steps.derives: If X_j is the set of pairs (S, lambda) defined in Lemma L3, then [q^j] F_{a,b,r}(q) = sum_{(S,lambda) in X_j} (-1)^(|S|).
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the coefficient formula asserted by Lemma L3 for the chosen a, b, r, j.

steps.derives: There exists an involution iota_j : X_j -> X_j such that non-fixed points change the parity of |S| and fixed points have even |S|.
steps.trivial_justification: Lemma L5 applies because A2 provides the required inequalities M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d, and the standing hypothesis gives 0 <= j <= floor(r(b-a)/2).

steps.derives: The signed sum sum_{(S,lambda) in X_j} (-1)^(|S|) is a nonnegative integer; equivalently, [q^j] F_{a,b,r}(q) is a nonnegative integer.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply Lemma L4 to the finite set X := X_j with sign function w(S,lambda) := (-1)^(|S|). By A4, the involution iota_j reverses the sign on every non-fixed point because it changes the parity of |S|, and every fixed point has sign +1 because A4 says fixed points have even |S|. Lemma L4 therefore gives sum_{(S,lambda) in X_j} (-1)^(|S|) = |Fix(iota_j)| >= 0. Then A3 identifies this same signed sum with [q^j] F_{a,b,r}(q).
Substitute the equality [q^j] R_{a,b,r}(q) = [q^j] F_{a,b,r}(q) from A1 into the nonnegativity result from A5.

steps.derives: For integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, let q be an indeterminate, define (q;q)_n := product_{t=1}^n (1 - q^t) for n >= 0 with (q;q)_0 := 1, set R_{a,b,r}(q) := ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b), and define D := r (b - a). Assume that R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q]. Then for every integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2), the coefficient of q^j in R_{a,b,r}(q) is a nonnegative integer.
steps.trivial_justification: The proof above was carried out for an arbitrary integer j satisfying 0 <= j <= floor(D/2), under the standing assumptions on a, b, r, q, and polynomiality of R_{a,b,r}(q). Universal generalization over that arbitrary j yields the desired statement for every j in the specified range, which is exactly the root theorem.
